questions.question: How can virtual reality assist in medical training when physical cadavers are difficult to obtain?
options: It provides interactive 2D diagrams of human anatomy
It provides immersive simulations of organs and how they work
It provides high-fidelity video recordings of surgeries
It provides real-time remote access to existing hospitals
questions.explanation: Virtual reality allows students to learn about body organs and their functions through immersive simulations, which is particularly useful when cadavers are scarce.

questions.question: How do non-immersive and fully immersive virtual reality systems differ regarding the user's sensory interaction?
options: Non-immersive systems require the user to be physically attached to the real world while fully immersive systems do not
Non-immersive systems provide a direct interaction between the virtual and physical environments while fully immersive ones do not
Non-immersive systems allow for real physical movements while fully immersive systems restrict physical movements to the virtual environment
Non-immersive systems allow the user to retain control of the physical environment while fully immersive systems block all senses
questions.explanation: Non-immersive systems are defined by the user retaining control of the physical environment, whereas fully immersive systems block all senses to replace the user's sense of reality with virtual realism.

questions.question: Why are semi-immersive systems the most common form of commercial virtual reality?
options: They are preferred because they allow users to perform real physical movements like running and jumping
They are the only systems that allow for three-dimensional virtual environments using headsets and other devices
They are cost-effective and provide partial immersion while leaving the user free to sense the real world
They are more popular because they allow for the complete replacement of reality with virtual realism
questions.explanation: Semi-immersive systems are the most common because they are cost-effective and provide a balance of partial immersion while leaving the user's other senses exposed to the real world.

questions.question: How is a user typically engaged in a non-immersive virtual reality application?
options: They are psychologically engaged and experience the real world while their eyes and ears remain open
They are physically attached to the real world but do not experience the virtual world at all
They are physically present in a virtual world while their eyes and ears are completely blocked by a headset
They are psychologically engaged and may not experience the real world while their eyes and ears remain open
questions.explanation: A non-immersive application takes away the user's attention so they are psychologically engaged, but the user's eyes, ears, and other organs remain open and connected to the real world.

data.text: Virtual reality systems are categorized into non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive systems based on the degree of sensory blocking they provide. Non-immersive systems engage the user psychologically while they remain physically attached to the real world, whereas semi-immersive systems offer a cost-effective middle ground by blocking some senses. Fully immersive systems provide the highest level of immersion by blocking all senses, though they are the most expensive and commercially rare.
points: Immersion in virtual reality means the user's senses are blocked so the user receives input only from the virtual world.
Virtual reality systems are broadly categorized into non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive systems based on their degree of immersion.
Non-immersive systems are specific computer applications that psychologically engage the user while they remain physically attached to the real world.
Semi-immersive systems are cost-effective systems that provide a partial immersive experience by blocking some but not all senses.
Fully immersive systems block all senses to replace the user's sense of reality with virtual realism.

questions.question: Why are semi-immersive virtual reality systems more common in commercial applications than fully immersive systems?
questions.reference_answer: Semi-immersive systems are the most commonly used form of VR because they are the most cost-effective. In contrast, fully immersive systems are commercially rare because they are difficult to afford.

questions.question: How does the blocking of senses differ between non-immersive and semi-immersive virtual reality systems?
questions.reference_answer: In a non-immersive system, the user's eyes, ears, and other sensory organs remain open and the user remains physically attached to the real world. A semi-immersive system provides a partial experience by blocking some but not all senses, such as blocking the eyes while leaving the ears and skin exposed to real-world signals.

questions.question: Why can the defense sector contribute significantly to the commercial value of extended reality despite representing a small percentage of application areas?
questions.reference_answer: Defense is a major application area for virtual reality training, including military medical and combat simulations. Although it may only account for about 4% of application areas, it represents a large monetary amount because worldwide military budgets are huge.
